sections.h2: How can I sell a house in Pemberton Township?
sections.html:
Three routes exist for a Pemberton house: an agent listing, a sale the owner runs alone, or a direct purchase by an investor who accepts the property in its present state. Condition and timing usually decide it, because the township wants its own inspection finished before title passes.

Browns Mills, Country Lake Estates, Pemberton Heights, Presidential Lakes Estates and part of Fort Dix all sit within the township. Pemberton borough is a separate municipality surrounded by the township, one of New Jersey's doughnut towns, so check which jurisdiction holds your parcel before you request forms.

  • Agent listing: reaches the most buyers, and puts showings, a buyer's home inspection and the township's resale inspection on your calendar.
  • Owner-run sale: keeps the commission, but you handle pricing, advertising and every municipal form yourself.
  • Investor purchase: a shorter path with fewer contingencies, and an offer priced for whatever repairs the buyer inherits.

Pemberton skews toward owners who stay put. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 27,611 people, up from 26,903 in April 2020, in 9,785 households of about 2.73 people each. Owners live in 73.3 percent of homes.

A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $234,500, well under the national typical value of $332,700, and household income runs $80,843 at the midpoint. Price your house against nearby sales, since a house needing work will draw offers shaped by what the buyer must fix.

sections.h2: Resale inspection before a Pemberton closing
sections.html:
A Certificate of Occupancy Transfer is required every time a residential unit gets a new occupant, and a sale counts. The seller submits a resale application to Code Enforcement along with the inspection fee.

Under the township's packet, the first inspection costs $150 and each repeat visit costs $50. Staff will not book a visit until the paperwork is complete and the fee is paid, and inspectors in the field cannot accept either. Applications lapse after 60 days, so file when a closing is realistic.

A buyer who wants to take over the certificate must tell the office in writing before it is issued. That option helps when the buyer plans repairs after closing. Code Enforcement answers at 609-894-3376. Items the inspector looks for include:

  • House numbers in reflective material, at least 3.5 inches tall, visible from the road.
  • Battery smoke detectors on every level, in each bedroom and outside sleeping areas, with carbon monoxide detectors near bedrooms where a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage exists.
  • An anti-tilt bracket on the stove, rails on stairs with four or more risers, and a mounted ABC extinguisher of 5 to 10 pounds.
  • Window screens, egress windows that open easily, and GFCI outlets in kitchens, baths, garages and outdoors.
  • Every utility switched on for the visit.

sections.h2: What else gets reviewed on the Pemberton resale application?
sections.html:
The form follows the account history of the property as well as the structure. Each department initials its own box, so clearing balances early keeps the file from stalling.

  • The tax office confirms liens, taxes paid, and the solid waste, water and sewer accounts.
  • Public Works notes the water and sewer units billed.
  • The housing office checks open permits, open code violations, vacant property fees and any board-up or clean-up charges.
  • Houses on private water or septic attach a well report or a septic report.

The attached checklist also tells you what Pemberton skips. Inspectors pass over air conditioning, pools, hot tubs and termites, turn away basements with standing water, and will not remove leftover furniture or appliances. For the roof, wiring, structure or heating, a bonded contractor's certification may be requested.

These are the figures a Pemberton seller meets most often.

sections.h2: Pemberton tax bills and your closing
sections.html:
Each installment is due on the first of its month, and a ten-day grace period runs to the 10th. After that, interest reaches back to the first. Balances left open on December 31 pick up a 6 percent year-end penalty on top.

One bill covers the township, Burlington County, the county farmland and open space fund, the local school board and the county library. Because the township collects for all five, a tax search before closing shows what is outstanding across the whole bill. Payments are credited on arrival, never by postmark, and a bill that never arrived is no excuse for a late installment. The tax office is at 609-894-3370.

A lien can be redeemed only by someone with a legal interest in the parcel. Requests go in writing to TaxOffice@pemberton-twp.com, and the payoff must arrive in full as certified funds. Title companies typically handle this step.

sections.h2: Do Pinelands rules touch a Pemberton sale?
sections.html:
They can. Pemberton is one of 56 southern New Jersey municipalities inside the Pinelands National Reserve, and part of the township lies in the narrower state-designated Pinelands Area. Congress created the reserve in 1978.

A plain change of ownership rarely hits those rules. They matter when a buyer wants an addition, a new outbuilding or a lot division. Ask the township's Community Development office whether your parcel is in the Pinelands Area before you make promises about future building.

sections.h2: State fee and Burlington County recording
sections.html:
The seller owes the state a realty transfer fee when the deed is recorded, set by bracket on the sale price. Nonresident sellers, including heirs who live elsewhere, also prepay Gross Income Tax at closing. That payment is the greater of a figure based on the gain and 2 percent of the price in the deed.

Burlington County's Clerk records the deed. Seller tax forms signed on or after October 1, 2025 must be the newest version, or the office returns them. The same office runs a free alert service that emails, texts or calls an owner when anything is recorded under their name. Call 609-265-5122 to ask about it. The county names seniors and owners of vacant properties as common targets of deed fraud.

sections.h2: When is a cash offer a good fit for a Pemberton house?
sections.html:
It suits a house that needs more work than the township checklist tolerates, a vacant property, or a seller with a firm move date. Ask any buyer who orders the transfer inspection, who pays the $150, and who signs for the repair list.

Judge an offer by what lands in your account after repairs, carrying costs and the state fee. Open permits and unpaid sewer or solid waste balances do not block a sale, though they have to be settled or credited at the table.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate of occupancy to sell my house in Pemberton Township?
faqs.a: Yes. Pemberton requires a Certificate of Occupancy Transfer when a residential unit changes occupant. The resale application lists a $150 first inspection, a $50 reinspection and a 60 day life.

faqs.q: Can a buyer take over the Pemberton certificate?
faqs.a: Yes, once the code office has that request in writing before it issues the certificate. The buyer then owns the repair list, which suits as-is and investor purchases.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Pemberton?
faqs.a: They are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a grace period to the 10th. After that, interest is 8 percent on the first $1,500 owed and 18 percent beyond it.

faqs.q: Who pays the state transfer fee on a Pemberton sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it at recording, in brackets that rise with the sale price. Your closing attorney can give you the exact amount.

faqs.q: Does Pemberton borough follow the township's sale rules?
faqs.a: Check before assuming so. The borough is its own municipality inside the township, so ask the office serving your address which set of forms and dates applies.
